description: We are a passionate and innovative team of students driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared interest in science and technology.
summary:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive web platform developed to facilitate the exploration and analysis of real astronomical data from NASA's SPHEREx mission, complemented by information from other scientific archives such as Gaia, AllWISE, and NEOWISE.
The platform allows users to study regions of the sky through tools such as Timelapse, image coaddition (COADD), subtraction of observations from different epochs, and spectral analysis. These features help visualize changes, improve the visibility of faint signals, and examine potential objects or phenomena of astronomical interest.
Additionally, the platform offers two user modes: an Observer, who can explore the available information, and a Scientist, who can also save searches and maintain records of their investigations.
Our project aims to make astronomical analysis tools accessible to a wider audience, simplify the interpretation of scientific data, and support the exploration of the infrared sky, contributing to the effective use of real data collected by space missions.
details:
SPHEREx Explorer — Project Details

What does our project do?

What if we could watch the infrared sky change over time?

SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive web platform that transforms real observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission into a visual experience.

By entering astronomical coordinates, users can explore regions of the sky and generate Timelapse animations to compare infrared observations captured on different dates.

The platform also offers image coaddition (COADD), epoch subtraction, spectral analysis, and overlays from Gaia DR3 and AllWISE. Additional infrared observations from WISE, NEOWISE, and unWISE provide more context for comparison.

What benefits does it offer?

Our platform brings multiple astronomical tools into one accessible environment, reducing the complexity of retrieving, processing, and comparing scientific data.

It offers two user modes: Observer, allowing anyone to explore without registration, and Scientist, enabling registered users to save searches, preserve results, and revisit previous investigations.

What is its intended impact?

We aim to make infrared astronomy more accessible to students, researchers, and curious minds worldwide.

By making temporal and spectral observations easier to understand, SPHEREx Explorer encourages scientific learning and helps users recognize changes in astronomical sources.

What technologies did we use?

We developed the platform using Python and JavaScript, supported by CSS, and Flask.

Python libraries such as NumPy, Astropy, PyVO, and reproject support astronomical data retrieval, image processing, and spatial alignment. JavaScript enables the interactive web experience.

Our platform uses real data from NASA/IPAC IRSA and complementary astronomical archives.

What makes our project creative?

Instead of displaying isolated astronomical images, we transform observations into an interactive journey through time.

By combining animations, infrared spectral information, image processing, and astronomical catalogs, users can explore the same region from multiple perspectives.

What factors did we consider?

We prioritized scientific accuracy, accessibility, and reliability.

Our design considers correct image alignment, observational coverage, data availability, and efficient retrieval through caching. We also distinguish visual comparisons from scientifically confirmed findings.

Our vision is simple: make the changing infrared sky something anyone can explore, understand, and experience.
